topSignals.title: NM Land Commissioner again blocks Project Jupiter gas pipeline through state lands; October 19 air permit hearing confirmed — compounding permit crisis for the 2.45 GW Bloom deployment
topSignals.text: — Two concurrent Project Jupiter setbacks not captured in the July 16–17 digests. First: on July 14, NM Commissioner of Public Lands Stephanie Garcia Richard denied Energy Transfer's reconsideration request for a ~0.6-mile right-of-way segment of the Green Chili Lateral pipeline through state trust lands — the second rejection (first was March 2026). The segment connects Project Jupiter to the existing El Paso Natural Gas pipeline; without it, the project must reroute the 17-mile, 24-inch pipeline or replace planned natural-gas fuel with an alternative. Garcia Richard cited minimal revenue to the trust (~$31,900 one-time + $43,400/year) versus significant greenhouse gas and water impacts. Energy Transfer has 30 days (from July 14) to file an administrative review petition. Second: NMED Secretary James Kenney confirmed the air quality permit hearing will be held at 9 a.m. on October 19, 2026 at the Sunland Park Multi-Generational Center; NMED has until November 23 to issue its permit decision. With both the gas-supply route and the air quality permit now in formal dispute, Project Jupiter Phase 1 (the single largest SOFC deployment in the pipeline) faces a realistic Q1 2027 slip. topSignals.title: Lazard 2026 LCOE+: CCGT LCOE rises to $90/MWh — 17-year high — narrowing the gap with ITC 48E-subsidized SOFC
topSignals.text: — Released July 13, 2026, the Lazard Levelized Cost of Energy+ 2026 report (the industry's leading annual LCOE benchmark) shows new-build combined-cycle gas turbine LCOE rising to $90/MWh, up from $78/MWh in 2025 and exceeding the previous high of $83/MWh set in 2009. Drivers: constrained gas turbine supply (GE Vernova 7H-series wait-lists extending to 2030+), tariff pass-through on steel and components, sustained interest rates, and supply-chain repricing from AI data center demand. SOFC implications are significant: with ITC 48E (30% capital credit), effective SOFC LCOE for a large-format Bloom EaaS deployment is approximately $90–140/MWh — now overlapping the lower bound of the Lazard CCGT range ($51–129/MWh, wide due to project variation). The traditional framing of "SOFC is more expensive than CCGT" is narrowing; for projects where speed-to-power (90 days vs. 24+ months), modularity, and NOx reduction are weighted, SOFC is now economically competitive with new-build CCGT at the margin. Note: this LCOE report was released July 13 but was not captured in the July 13–17 digests. topSignals.title: BE holds near $210 Saturday — 10 days to Q2 earnings; market repricing execution risk, not technology
topSignals.text: — After closing at $206.73 on July 16 (first close below the Wells Fargo $217 bear case, -13.64% on the day despite the $1.7B Oaktree/IDF Nebius announcement), Bloom Energy stabilized at approximately $210 on July 17 before markets closed for the weekend. Today (July 18) is Saturday; no trading. The divergence between deal flow ($1.7B institutional project finance closed, Brookfield $25B framework, Oracle 2.45 GW, Crusoe 900 MW) and stock price (-41% from the $351 ATH) is now extreme. Q2 earnings on July 28 (AH) — consensus: $804M revenue / $0.36 EPS / ~34% gross margin — have become the sole reset event. Three active short-seller theses remain outstanding (Hunterbrook scandium supply chain, Crossroads Capital "supply wall," Doomberg trade-data analysis), all unresolved ahead of the print. items.text: EFCF proceedings: day 15 embargo — Still no technical results from the 17th European SOFC & SOE Forum (closed July 3, Lucerne). Elcogen (E3000 G2: stated ≥75% electrical / ≥90% CHP at 650°C), Ceres licensees (Doosan yield trajectory vs. 90% target), SolydEra, and Convion have published nothing online. Fifteen days post-conference exceeds any precedent for this event; a coordinated journal submission embargo is confirmed. Monitor elcogen.com, ceres.tech, solydera.com, convion.fi. EFCF 2026

Quiet otherwise. Background: Bloom Fremont 2 GW ramp (cost-per-kW update expected July 28); UMD 4 W/cm² at 650°C ceria electrolyte breakthrough (July 13); Mico Power CE certification for 2 kW H2 SOFC (first Korean CE-certified direct-H2 SOFC, A+ ErP rating) — all covered in prior digests.

Project Jupiter (2.45 GW, Oracle/OpenAI, NM) — dual permit crisis — See Top Signal #1. October 19 air permit hearing confirmed (NMED decision Nov. 23) plus second pipeline denial through state lands compounds the Phase 1 delivery risk. Energy Transfer's 30-day administrative review window runs to approximately August 13. If Energy Transfer files and loses, the pipeline must be rerouted around state trust land (~0.6 miles of alternative routing required), adding weeks to months to the construction schedule. The combination of air permit hearing (Oct. 19) + potential pipeline reroute is the single largest near-term execution risk in the SOFC deployment pipeline. Source NM — pipeline | PGJ Online — pipeline denial

Active pipeline otherwise unchanged: Crusoe/Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1 (H2 2026), FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW (30 MW initial delivery H2 2026), Equinix >100 MW, AEP/Bloom 1 GW (Wyoming, 2030), Bloom/Brookfield $25B EaaS, Nebius 328 MW EaaS ($1.7B Oaktree/IDF project finance closed July 16).

FERC Generation Adequacy Reports: Monday July 20 (2 days) — The six RTO/ISO informational reports mandated by FERC's June 18 Section 206 show-cause orders are due Monday. Each grid operator (PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, NYISO, ISO-NE) must quantify how adequate generation will serve new and existing large loads (≥50 MW on ≥69 kV), including stakeholder proposals and milestone schedules. ISO-NE's 90-day abeyance request would push its response to ~August 3 if granted. Full tariff reform or show-cause justifications due August 17. Monday's filings will be the first regulator-mandated public estimates of the firm-power gap by US grid region — the primary external upper-bound sizing of the SOFC grid-bypass addressable market. FERC RM26-4

Background unchanged: Virginia DC electricity tax $0.011/kWh in force (self-generated SOFC not exempt, from July 1); Germany EnEfG 4-year PUE compliance window (cabinet adoption June 24, Bundestag/Bundesrat approval pending); EU CADA energy efficiency rating scheme delayed into Q3; Section 179D sunset confirmed June 30; ITC 48E 30% fuel cell credit active.
Quiet weekend. No new SMR, CCGT, or battery announcements.

Lazard 2026: CCGT cost pressure — See Top Signal #2. At $90/MWh new-build CCGT LCOE and long equipment lead times, the traditional "CCGT is cheaper" argument is eroding. Projects needing power before 2028 have a narrowing competitive alternative to SOFC. Background: Microsoft Project Kilby 2.67 GW CCGT (Texas, first power 2028 — ordered before the current cost spike), GE Vernova/Blue Energy 2.5 GW gas-plus-nuclear Texas (gas ~2030, nuclear ~2032), Microsoft TMI/Crane Center 835 MW nuclear (H2 2027) — all covered in prior digests.

lcoe.text: Lazard 2026: CCGT LCOE $90/MWh — update CCGT benchmark in model — Revise the CCGT LCOE comparison from the $45–100/MWh range previously modeled to $51–129/MWh (full range) with a central case of $90/MWh for new-build in 2026. At $90/MWh CCGT and SOFC at $90–140/MWh (with ITC 48E and CHP credit), the SOFC cost premium is now $0–50/MWh on a like-for-like basis — substantially narrower than the prior $45–95/MWh gap. The premium disappears entirely for Virginia or Texas projects where CCGT lead times (2028 earliest), gas turbine scarcity, and transmission charges must be added. Lazard

Project Jupiter compounding risk — add scenario: Oracle/Bloom 2.45 GW delayed to Q2 2027 — With October 19 air permit hearing (NMED decision Nov. 23) AND pipeline reroute risk (Energy Transfer 30-day petition window to ~Aug. 13), the earliest plausible Phase 1 delivery is Q1–Q2 2027. Model impact: approximately $400–700M of FY2026 Bloom revenue at risk from timing slip. Recommend flagging two scenarios: (a) Permit approved Nov. 23, first power Q1 2027; (b) Appeal delays NMED to Q1 2027 + pipeline reroute adds 60–90 days → first power Q3 2027. Add as a revenue-timing sensitivity in the LCOE project cashflow model.

FERC reports Monday (July 20) — SOFC addressable market upper bound — Extract firm-power gap by RTO/ISO from the five filed reports (ISO-NE may defer). Key metric: total confirmed large-load MW seeking grid connection that cannot be served within 5 years per region. This sets the de facto market ceiling for SOFC grid-bypass. Mark as an immediate update trigger.

Primary LCOE model update trigger: July 28 BE Q2 earnings (AH) — 10 days — Five inputs: (a) manufacturing cost per kW at 2 GW Fremont run rate, (b) product gross margin vs. ~34% guidance, (c) scandium/supply-chain sourcing transparency (Hunterbrook resolution), (d) Project Jupiter permit update + Oracle pipeline commentary, (e) EaaS $/MWh pricing from the Nebius $1.7B deployment. Lazard 2026 CCGT benchmark ($90/MWh) should be incorporated in the same model refresh.
